journal_name: ACM Transactions on Privacy and Security

abstracts.abstract: The proliferation of quantum computing poses unprecedented threats to classical cryptographic primitives underlying existing privacy-preserving protocols. This paper introduces a novel paradigm for privacy computation termed Lattice-Based Compositional Privacy (LBCP), which fundamentally reconceptualizes the relationship between security and privacy in post-quantum settings. Unlike conventional approaches that retrofit classical techniques with quantum-resistant components, LBCP integrates lattice-based cryptography directly into the privacy definition itself. We propose a comprehensive security model in the universal composability framework, demonstrating that LBCP achieves indistinguishability under chosen-ciphertext attacks while simultaneously satisfying a strengthened notion of differential privacy. Our analysis establishes formal connections between the hardness of the Learning With Errors problem and privacy leakage bounds, revealing that LBCP provides exponentially improved privacy guarantees compared to existing proposals when confronting quantum adversaries. Furthermore, we introduce a modular composition theorem that enables LBCP protocols to preserve privacy properties across arbitrarily complex protocol interactions. This work opens a new theoretical direction by establishing that cryptographic security and privacy protection can be mutually reinforcing rather than competing objectives, fundamentally shifting the paradigm for designing privacy-preserving systems in the quantum era.

Classical differential privacy mechanisms suffer from significant limitations in handling high-dimensional data with correlated attributes, resulting in excessive privacy budget consumption and diminished utility. This paper presents an Adaptive Composition Framework for Correlated Data (ACF-CD) that substantially improves upon existing approaches by incorporating covariance-aware privacy budget allocation. Our key insight is that traditional composition theorems underestimate privacy preservation in correlated settings, leading to overly conservative privacy guarantees. We develop a novel privacy accounting method based on the concept of zero-concentrated differential privacy with correlation factors, providing tighter composition bounds that adapt to the underlying data structure. Theoretically, we prove that ACF-CD achieves (ε, δ)-differential privacy with a 35% reduction in privacy budget consumption compared to standard advanced composition while maintaining the same utility guarantees. Our framework introduces efficient algorithms for computing correlation-adjusted sensitivity and optimal noise calibration that operate in near-linear time. Experimental validation on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates that ACF-CD enables significantly more accurate statistical analysis and machine learning tasks under identical privacy constraints, particularly for datasets exhibiting complex correlation patterns.

Cross-organizational data collaboration faces fundamental tensions between privacy protection, regulatory compliance, and computational efficiency. This paper presents PriChain, a blockchain-based privacy-preserving data sharing platform that fundamentally reimagines secure computation as a decentralized service. Unlike existing systems that treat privacy and computation as separate concerns requiring post-hoc integration, PriChain embeds privacy guarantees directly into the computational infrastructure through a novel three-layer architecture: a privacy-preserving execution layer using secure multi-party computation, a verifiable computation layer employing zero-knowledge proofs, and a decentralized governance layer implemented via smart contracts. This architectural paradigm ensures that privacy properties are enforced at the protocol level rather than relying on trusted intermediaries. We implement a complete prototype supporting standard SQL-like queries and machine learning model training, demonstrating practical applicability across healthcare, finance, and IoT domains. Security analysis proves that PriChain provides Byzantine fault tolerance and prevents information leakage even under colluding adversary models. Performance evaluation on benchmark datasets reveals that our system achieves practical throughput for real-world workloads while maintaining cryptographic privacy guarantees, representing a paradigm shift toward universally deployable privacy-preserving computation infrastructure.

Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) systems face increasing challenges in dynamic environments where access policies must adapt to evolving contexts while protecting sensitive attribute information from unauthorized disclosure. This paper presents EnhanceABAC, an enhanced ABAC system that significantly improves both privacy protection and policy evaluation efficiency through the integration of attribute-based encryption with lightweight verifiable computation. The key improvement over prior work lies in our novel attribute encoding scheme that reduces ciphertext size by 60% while maintaining full policy expressiveness. Our system architecture comprises three optimized components: a distributed attribute authority managing credentials with privacy-preserving updates, an efficient policy evaluation engine leveraging outsourced computation with verifiable guarantees, and a lightweight client library enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. We provide comprehensive security proofs demonstrating that EnhanceABAC prevents attribute leakage under adaptive corruption models while maintaining standard authorization soundness. Implementation and extensive evaluation across diverse policy scenarios reveal that our system achieves 40% faster policy evaluation compared to state-of-the-art encrypted ABAC systems, with particularly pronounced improvements in complex policy environments containing hundreds of attributes. This work delivers practical privacy-preserving access control suitable for deployment in enterprise cloud environments and emerging edge computing scenarios.
